concepts.description: Matter structure whose internal electrons, energy levels, and spectra are modeled by quantum mechanics.
concepts.label: atom

concepts.description: Mathematical constraint on correlations implied by local hidden-variable theories.
concepts.label: Bell inequality

concepts.description: Radiation characterized by a curve of light intensity across frequencies from hot objects.
concepts.label: black-body radiation

concepts.description: Physics describing matter and energy at scales familiar from human experience.
concepts.label: classical physics

concepts.description: Interpretation stating that before measurement, statements about a particle's properties are completely meaningless.
concepts.label: Copenhagen interpretation

concepts.description: Requirement that quantum theory converge to classical limits at macroscopic scales.
concepts.label: correspondence principle

concepts.description: Relativistic wave equation for electrons that incorporates relativity and predicts antimatter.
concepts.label: Dirac wave equation

concepts.description: Experiment in which particles or waves passing through two slits produce an interference pattern.
concepts.label: double-slit experiment

concepts.description: State in which an object has a definite value for a specified property or measurement.
concepts.label: eigenstate

concepts.description: Definite value associated with an eigenstate of a quantum property.
concepts.label: eigenvalue

concepts.description: Corpuscular particle whose properties and behavior are central to the quantum phenomena described.
concepts.label: electron

concepts.description: Technological application of quantum mechanics.
concepts.label: electron microscope

concepts.description: Discrete unit of energy proposed for light and used to explain black-body radiation and the photoelectric effect.
concepts.label: energy quantum

concepts.description: Pattern of alternating light and dark bands produced by wave interference and reproduced by quantum particles statistically.
concepts.label: interference pattern

concepts.description: Technological application of quantum mechanics.
concepts.label: laser

concepts.description: Theory in which measurement outcomes depend on hidden variables local to each separated particle.
concepts.label: local hidden-variable theory

concepts.description: Technological application of quantum mechanics.
concepts.label: magnetic resonance imaging

concepts.description: Interpretation describing a multiverse containing every possible universe.
concepts.label: many-worlds interpretation

concepts.description: Principle that two electrons in an atom cannot have the same set of quantum numbers.
concepts.label: Pauli exclusion principle

concepts.description: Ejection of electrons from a metal surface when illuminated, with electron number depending on light intensity and velocity on frequency.
concepts.label: photoelectric effect

concepts.description: Quantum or smallest observable particle of the electromagnetic field.
concepts.label: photon

concepts.description: Principle that a quantum system displays wave-like or particle-like properties according to the measurement performed.
concepts.label: principle of complementarity

concepts.description: Restriction of physical quantities or energies to discrete allowable values.
concepts.label: quantization

aliases: quantum theory of the electromagnetic force
concepts.description: Quantum field theory of the electromagnetic force.
concepts.label: quantum electrodynamics

concepts.description: Condition in which the quantum state of particles cannot be described independently, including when they are widely separated.
concepts.label: quantum entanglement

concepts.description: Field treated within quantum theory, including the electromagnetic field whose quantum is the photon.
concepts.label: quantum field

concepts.description: Quantum theory of fields that permits particle creation and annihilation.
concepts.label: quantum field theory

concepts.description: Study and theory of matter and its interactions with energy at atomic and subatomic scales.
concepts.label: quantum mechanics

concepts.description: The shift from classical physical models to quantum mechanics prompted by phenomena classical physics could not explain.
concepts.label: quantum revolution

concepts.description: Quantum process allowing electrons to penetrate a potential barrier.
concepts.label: quantum tunneling

concepts.description: Formula predicting the distinctive absorption-line frequencies of hydrogen gas.
concepts.label: Rydberg formula

concepts.description: Quantum degree of freedom associated with electrons and discrete magnetic behavior of atoms.
concepts.label: spin

concepts.description: Quantum field theory describing three fundamental forces and classifying known elementary particles.
concepts.label: Standard Model

concepts.description: Experiment in which a beam of atoms separates into two streams in a magnetic field, demonstrating quantized spin states.
concepts.label: Stern–Gerlach experiment

concepts.description: Macroscopic quantum phenomenon and technological application of quantum mechanics.
concepts.label: superconductor

concepts.description: Quantum phenomenon in which liquid helium near absolute zero spontaneously flows up and over its container rim.
concepts.label: superfluidity

concepts.description: Quantum-mechanical technological component used in modern electronics.
concepts.label: transistor

concepts.description: Principle that certain properties, such as position and momentum, cannot be simultaneously measured or defined to arbitrary precision.
concepts.label: uncertainty principle

concepts.description: Quantum description of a system's probabilistic or potential state.
concepts.label: wave function

concepts.description: Conversion of a probabilistic quantum state into a definite measured value through measurement.
concepts.label: wave function collapse

concepts.description: Principle that photons and matter exhibit both wave-like and particle-like behavior, neither classical description being sufficient alone.
concepts.label: wave–particle duality

evidence.quote: a beam of light is directed through two narrow, closely spaced slits, producing an interference pattern of light and dark bands on a screen.

grounded_assertions.statement: In the double-slit experiment, light passing through two slits produces an interference pattern of light and dark bands.

evidence.quote: By 1889, the Rydberg formula predicted the lines for hydrogen gas using only a constant number and the integers to index the lines.

grounded_assertions.statement: The Rydberg formula predicted the absorption lines of hydrogen gas using a constant and integers indexing the lines.

evidence.quote: The concept of wave–particle duality says that neither the classical concept of "particle" nor of "wave" can fully describe the behavior of quantum-scale objects, either photons or matter.

grounded_assertions.statement: Wave–particle duality states that neither the classical concept of a particle nor that of a wave fully describes photons or matter.

evidence.quote: Variations of the double-slit experiment have been performed using electrons, atoms, and even large molecules, and the same type of interference pattern is seen.

grounded_assertions.statement: Variations of the double-slit experiment using electrons, atoms, and large molecules produce the same type of interference pattern.

evidence.quote: When an object can definitely be "pinned-down" in some respect, it is said to possess an eigenstate.

grounded_assertions.statement: An object with a definite value for a property is said to possess an eigenstate.

evidence.quote: Quantum mechanics is the study of matter and matter's interactions with energy on the scale of atomic and subatomic particles.

grounded_assertions.statement: Quantum mechanics studies matter and its interactions with energy at atomic and subatomic scales.

evidence.quote: scientists discovered phenomena in both the large (macro) and the small (micro) worlds that classical physics could not explain. The desire to resolve inconsistencies between observed phenomena and classical theory led to a revolution in physics, a shift in the original scientific paradigm: the development of quantum mechanics.

grounded_assertions.statement: Classical physics could not explain some phenomena discovered in the macro and micro worlds, contributing to the development of quantum mechanics.

evidence.quote: The Standard Model of particle physics is the quantum field theory that describes three of the four known fundamental forces in the universe (electromagnetic, weak and strong interactions but not gravity) and classifies all known elementary particles.

grounded_assertions.statement: The Standard Model is a quantum field theory that describes three fundamental forces and classifies known elementary particles.

evidence.quote: Wave function collapse means that a measurement has forced or converted a quantum (probabilistic or potential) state into a definite measured value.

grounded_assertions.statement: Wave function collapse converts a probabilistic or potential quantum state into a definite measured value.

evidence.quote: This concept was formalized by Bohr in 1923 as the correspondence principle. It requires quantum theory to converge to classical limits.

grounded_assertions.statement: The correspondence principle requires quantum theory to converge to classical limits.

evidence.quote: Quantum mechanics helps people understand chemistry because it explains how atoms interact with each other and form molecules.

grounded_assertions.statement: Quantum mechanics explains how atoms interact with each other and form molecules.

evidence.quote: Instead, the beam separated into two, and only two, diverging streams of atoms.

grounded_assertions.statement: The Stern–Gerlach experiment showed that a beam of atoms separates into two streams in a magnetic field rather than a continuous range of directions.

evidence.quote: Quantum mechanics shows that certain pairs of physical properties, for example, position and speed, cannot be simultaneously measured, nor defined in operational terms, to arbitrary precision

grounded_assertions.statement: The uncertainty principle states that certain pairs of physical properties, such as position and speed, cannot be simultaneously measured or defined to arbitrary precision.

evidence.quote: if liquid helium cooled to a temperature near absolute zero is placed in a container, it spontaneously flows up and over the rim of its container; this is an effect that cannot be explained by classical physics.

grounded_assertions.statement: Superfluidity is described as a phenomenon in which liquid helium near absolute zero spontaneously flows up and over the rim of its container, an effect classical physics cannot explain.

evidence.quote: a group of particles can interact or be created together in such a way that the quantum state of each particle of the group cannot be described independently of the state of the others, including when the particles are separated by a large distance. This is known as quantum entanglement.

grounded_assertions.statement: Quantum entanglement occurs when the quantum state of each particle in a group cannot be described independently of the states of the other particles, even when they are widely separated.

evidence.quote: Max Planck, unconvinced by the atomic theory, discovered that he needed discrete entities like atoms or electrons to explain black-body radiation.
Planck spread the heat energy among individual "oscillators" of an undefined character but with discrete energy capacity; this model explained black-body radiation.

grounded_assertions.statement: Planck used discrete energy entities to explain black-body radiation.

evidence.quote: In even a simple light switch, quantum tunneling is absolutely vital, as otherwise the electrons in the electric current could not penetrate the potential barrier made up of a layer of oxide.

grounded_assertions.statement: Quantum tunneling is vital to a simple light switch because electrons in the electric current must penetrate an oxide potential barrier.

evidence.quote: Lenard showed that the amount of current – the number of electrons – depended on the intensity of the light, but that the velocity of these electrons did not depend on intensity. This is the photoelectric effect.

grounded_assertions.statement: In the photoelectric effect, the number of electrons emitted depends on light intensity, while their velocity does not depend on intensity.

evidence.quote: Paul Dirac published his relativistic wave equation simultaneously incorporating relativity, predicting anti-matter, and providing a complete theory for the Stern–Gerlach result.

grounded_assertions.statement: The Dirac wave equation incorporated relativity, predicted antimatter, and provided a complete theory for the Stern–Gerlach result.

evidence.quote: QFT ... goes a step further and allows for the creation and annihilation of particles

grounded_assertions.statement: Quantum field theory allows the creation and annihilation of particles.

evidence.quote: There cannot exist an atom in such a quantum state that two electrons within [it] have the same set of quantum numbers.

grounded_assertions.statement: The Pauli exclusion principle states that two electrons within an atom cannot have the same set of quantum numbers.

evidence.quote: Applications of quantum mechanics include the laser, the transistor, the electron microscope, and magnetic resonance imaging.

grounded_assertions.statement: Applications of quantum mechanics include lasers, transistors, electron microscopes, and magnetic resonance imaging.

evidence.quote: Quantum electrodynamics (QED) is the name of the quantum theory of the electromagnetic force.

grounded_assertions.statement: Quantum electrodynamics is the quantum theory of the electromagnetic force.

evidence.quote: Albert Einstein proposed that light was also corpuscular, consisting of "energy quanta", in contradiction to the established science of light as a continuous wave

grounded_assertions.statement: Einstein proposed that light consists of energy quanta rather than being only a continuous wave.
